stories.name: Silas Contaifer
stories.location: Richmond, Virginia, USA (originally from Brasília, Brazil)
stories.story_summary:
Brazilian-born VCU pharmacy PhD student Silas Contaifer placed an Insta360 Pro inside a sterile compounding cleanroom to create VR 360 training videos for second-year pharmacists learning aseptic technique (2024).
• A guy who started with environmental management and habitat mapping in Brazil ended up teaching American pharmacy students how to gown up for cleanrooms — via a 360-degree camera on a tripod
• Insta360 relevance: First published pharmacy education use case for Insta360. Completes a pattern across healthcare: neurosurgery (Japan), oncology (Stanford), psychiatry (Denmark, Ukraine), stroke rehab (Beijing), and now pharmacy (Virginia). Enterprise team should note the breadth.
• His lab's philosophy: 'Everyone leaves my lab with some system they can use in their work.' He's built VR surgical planning tools, ER simulations, and AI-powered 3D body models alongside this project
• Moving to Italy post-graduation to work as a medical science liaison while maintaining research connections between VCU and Brazil's Federal University of São Paulo
stories.why_it_matters: First peer-reviewed pharmacy education study to use an Insta360 camera. The researcher's broader VR/XR portfolio positions him as a long-term contact for Insta360 in healthcare education.
stories.source_quote: An Insta360 Pro camera was placed in various locations around the sterile compounding cleanroom suite.
stories.source_type: peer-reviewed academic journal (Journal of Pharmacy Technology, 2024)
stories.verification_note: Insta360 Pro explicitly named in search snippets from PMC (PMC10959084) and SAGE Journals. Published 2024. Source returns 403 on WebFetch (bot-detection). Camera model older (Insta360 Pro, 2017/2018, discontinued). NOTE: 7th medical/academic VR story in database — pattern is real but domains keep diversifying (this is pharmacy, first time). Researcher profile confirmed via VCU News May 2025 feature. Not on exclusion list.
